subject: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype — status, p95 deltas, and decision timeline (ADR sign-off)

body:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 8:42 AM
Subject: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype — status, p95 deltas, and decision timeline (ADR sign-off)

Lauren —

Can you send me a crisp status on the mixed-workload scheduler prototype?

Specifically:
- p95 deltas (short/interactive) vs baseline in the mixed prompt distributions we care about
- any throughput/regression trade-offs we’re seeing
- decision timeline for whether we keep it as a flag vs graduate for a tier/route
- what you need from me for ADR sign-off

Trying to get this into my weekly staff update with something quantifiable.

Thanks,
Ava
CTO, Redwood Inference



From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 10:13 AM
Subject: Re: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype — status, p95 deltas, and decision timeline (ADR sign-off)

Ava —

TL;DR: Prototype is doing what we want for the “chat under summarization” pattern. Biggest remaining work is tightening rollback criteria + ensuring long-prompt fairness signals are front-and-center during canary.

Quantifiable deltas (latest A/B on perf-canary; runtime-1.19 build, flag ON vs OFF):
1) Mixed workload (70% short chat prompts, 30% long-context summarization; bursty arrivals)
- Short requests (TTFT): p95 improved ~28% (420ms -> 300ms), p99 improved ~22% (760ms -> 590ms)
- End-to-end latency (short): p95 improved ~19% (1.90s -> 1.54s)
- Long requests: p95 flat to slightly worse (+2–5% depending on batch shape) but within our guardrail
- Aggregate throughput: -2.7% (mostly due to fairness window forcing periodic long-queue service)

2) “Worst-case” distribution (50/50 short vs very-long prompts; long prompts near our max context)
- Short TTFT p95 improved ~17% (510ms -> 425ms)
- Throughput impact: -4.5% (this is the scenario we’re watching)
- No starvation observed in sim harness; long-queue max wait stayed under the configured bound in the runs we’ve done

3) Short-only workload (control)
- Within noise (p95 +/- 1–2%); no material regression

Trade-offs / risks (current):
- Misclassification can hurt: if a “long-ish” prompt gets tagged short, it can still trigger a prefill-heavy batch and cause a local spike. The latest classifier tweaks reduce this, but we should treat it as a known issue during canary.
- Under sustained overload, backpressure behavior is improved vs baseline, but we need SRE to confirm alert thresholds and paging policy are sane.

Decision timeline (proposal):
- Thu/Fri (this week): ADR sign-off (ADR-0147) to proceed with staged canary + define graduation criteria
- Next week: limited production slice (Dedicated only, 1–2% of traffic in us-east) with the flag ON, default remains OFF
- Week after: go/no-go to expand the slice (up to 10%) OR keep as opt-in for specific tiers/routes depending on throughput trade-off + customer feedback

What I need from you:
- Sign-off on ADR-0147 framing: we’re choosing “two-queue short-first with fairness window + max-wait bound” over SRPT-like approximation for operational predictability.
- Alignment on the graduation bar: we’re currently targeting “>=15% p95 TTFT improvement on short traffic in mixed workloads with <=5% throughput regression” as the primary gate.

Attaching the 1-page exec summary and the perf-canary A/B table extract.

Best,
Lauren
PM, Dedicated & Performance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: MixedWorkloadScheduler_ExecSummary_v3.pdf
Attachment: PerfCanary_ABSummary_2025-01-15.csv



From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 11:02 AM
Subject: Re: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype — status, p95 deltas, and decision timeline (ADR sign-off)

This is helpful.

Two asks:
1) Please make sure the ADR explicitly calls out the throughput regression tolerance and the “no starvation” definition (what metric + what bound). I don’t want us hand-waving fairness in the exec review.
2) Neha — can you confirm the rollback triggers you want in place for the limited prod slice? I want those listed in the ADR as well.

If you can incorporate those, I’m fine signing ADR-0147 this week.

Ava



From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 12:19 PM
Subject: Re: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype — status, p95 deltas, and decision timeline (ADR sign-off)

Looping in with the SRE view.

For the limited production slice (Dedicated, us-east, 1–2%), I want rollback criteria that are simple and unambiguous. Proposed triggers (any one triggers rollback):

A) Tail latency regression (short class)
- Short TTFT p95 > baseline + 10% for 15 minutes (rolling)
OR
- Short end-to-end p99 > baseline + 10% for 15 minutes

B) Queue health / starvation signals
- Long-queue max wait time > configured bound (we should set an explicit number; suggestion: 30s) in >1% of requests over 10 minutes
OR
- Long queue depth monotonically increasing for 20 minutes with stable incoming rate (proxy for starvation/backpressure mismatch)

C) Error budget / availability
- Elevated timeout rate (+0.3% absolute) sustained for 10 minutes on the canary slice

Operational notes:
- Canary must ship with the per-class queue depth + wait time panels pinned and alerting enabled (we can keep alerts scoped to the canary label to avoid paging the world).
- Rollback should be “flip flag off” only. No config edits, no redeploy required.

Lauren: if you paste these into the ADR + canary plan, SRE will sign off.

Neha Kapoor
SRE Leadership
Redwood Inference



From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 17, 2025 at 3:18 PM
Subject: Re: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype — status, p95 deltas, and decision timeline (ADR sign-off)

Ava —

Done. I updated ADR-0147 with:
- Graduation gate: >=15% short TTFT p95 improvement in mixed workloads, <=5% throughput regression, and no increase in timeout/error rate beyond the canary thresholds
- Fairness definition: “long-queue max wait time bound” (proposal: 30s) + monitoring on % of requests exceeding the bound
- Explicit rollback triggers per Neha’s note

Can you add your approval on the ADR (comment is fine) by EOD today? If we have that, we’ll keep the timeline as: start limited canary Monday, first readout mid-week, decision checkpoint end of week.

Thanks,
Lauren
